results.name: Exercise Ball Leg Curl
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms at your sides, palms facing down. Place your heels and calves on top of an exercise ball.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your heels. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees and roll the ball towards your glutes by pulling your heels in. Keep your hips elevated and maintain the straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Slowly extend your legs, rolling the ball back to the starting position while keeping your hips lifted. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide stability and ease of movement.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you curl the ball in and inhaling as you extend your legs.
results.description: Exercise Ball Leg Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl
instructions: Begin by lying on your back with your arms at your sides, palms facing down. Place your left heel and calf on top of an exercise ball, with your right leg extended straight and aligned with your hips.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your left heel.
Bend your left knee and roll the ball diagonally towards the middle of your hips, pulling your heel in while simultaneously raising your right leg upwards along the line of your hips.
Extend your left leg, rolling the ball back to the starting position, while lowering your right leg back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the movement with your right heel and calf on the ball and your left leg extending upwards.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you curl the ball in and inhale as you extend your leg.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide stability and ease of movement.
results.description: Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Exercise Ball Wall Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place an exercise ball between your lower back and a wall. Lean slightly into the ball for support.
Slowly lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and allowing the ball to roll along your back.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor, ensuring your knees do not extend past your toes.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, straightening your legs. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your feet are positioned far enough in front of you so that your knees do not extend past your toes when squatting.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, inhaling as you lower into the squat and exhaling as you push back up.
Maintain an upright posture with your back against the ball to avoid leaning forward.
results.description: Exercise Ball Wall Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Feet Together Barbell Squats
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a barbell across your upper back with an overhand grip. Ensure the barbell is balanced and rests comfortably on your traps.
Slowly lower your body into a squat by bending your knees and hips, keeping your knees aligned with your toes.
Lower yourself until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as your flexibility allows, without compromising form.
Push through your heels to stand back up, extending your knees and hips to return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your feet together throughout the entire movement to maintain balance and stability.
Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward.
Maintain a neutral spine and keep your chest up to avoid rounding your back.
results.description: Feet Together Barbell Squats is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Calves.

results.name: Fire Hydrant Bodyweight
instructions: Begin on the floor in an all-fours position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle, lift your right leg out to the side until your thigh is parallel to the floor. Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso.
Hold the position for a moment, then lower your right leg back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left leg and repeat.
tips: Avoid rotating your hips or torso; focus on isolating the movement in your hip.
Perform the exercise on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your leg and inhaling as you lower it.
Ensure your hands are positioned directly under your shoulders to maintain proper form and prevent strain.
results.description: Fire Hydrant Bodyweight is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors.

results.name: Fire Hydrant Circle Bodyweight
instructions: Begin on the floor in an all-fours position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle, lift your right leg out to the side until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Move your right leg in a circular motion, making small controlled circles with your knee while keeping your hips level and avoiding torso rotation.
Complete the desired number of circles, then lower your right leg back to the starting position. Repeat on the left side.
tips: Avoid rotating your hips or torso; focus on isolating the movement in your hip.
Perform the exercise on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your leg and inhaling as you lower it.
Ensure your hands are positioned directly under your shoulders to maintain proper form and prevent strain.
results.description: Fire Hydrant Circle Bodyweight is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors.

results.name: Frog Jumps
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width apart and your toes turned slightly outward. Lower into a deep squat and reach both hands toward the floor between your feet.
Push through your feet and jump straight upward, extending your hips and knees.
Land softly in the same wide stance and immediately bend your knees.
Lower back into the squat, reach toward the floor, and continue repeating the movement.
tips: Keep your chest lifted and avoid rounding your lower back in the squat.
Bend your knees immediately upon landing to absorb the impact.
Fully extend your hips and knees at the top of each jump.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you jump upward.
results.description: Frog Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Adductors.

results.name: Front Squats Dumbbell Low
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, hanging by your sides, with your palms facing each other.
Lower your body into a squat by bending your knees and hinging at your hips, pushing your knees lightly outwards as you descend.
Continue lowering yourself until your thighs are just lower than parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward during the squat.
Maintain a straight back and avoid leaning forward excessively.
Keep your chest up and your shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
results.description: Front Squats Dumbbell Low is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Front Squats Dumbbell Over Shoulders
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Position the dumbbells over your shoulders with your palms facing forward and elbows pointing down.
Lower your body into a squat by bending your knees and hinging at your hips, pushing your knees lightly outwards as you descend.
Continue lowering yourself until your thighs are just lower than parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward during the squat.
Maintain a straight back and avoid leaning forward excessively.
Keep your chest up and your shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
results.description: Front Squats Dumbbell Over Shoulders is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Glute Bridge Bodyweight
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Brace your core and press through your heels.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower and repeat.
tips: Don't arch your lower back at the top.
Keep your knees in line with your feet.
results.description: Glute Bridge Bodyweight is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core.
